chapters.title: The gospel begins with power and compassion

parts.text: John prepares the Lord’s way by preaching repentance and baptizing those confessing their sins. He announces one greater who will baptize with the Holy Ghost. Jesus is baptized, the Spirit descends, and the Father declares him his beloved Son. After temptation in the wilderness and John’s imprisonment, Jesus preaches the approaching kingdom and calls four fishermen to follow him.

In Capernaum, his authoritative teaching and expulsion of an unclean spirit astonish the people. He heals Simon’s mother-in-law and many others, then withdraws early to pray. He continues preaching through Galilee and cleanses a leper, directing him to the priest. The man’s public reports draw such crowds that Jesus remains outside the towns, where people still come to him.

Four men lower a paralyzed man through a roof to reach Jesus. Seeing their faith, he forgives the man’s sins, then heals him to demonstrate his authority when scribes object. Jesus calls Levi from the receipt of custom and shares a meal with publicans (tax collectors) and sinners. He explains that the sick need a physician and that he has come to call sinners to repentance.

Questions about fasting lead Jesus to speak of the bridegroom’s presence, new cloth, and new wine. When critics object to his disciples plucking grain on the sabbath, he recalls David eating the shewbread in need. He declares that the sabbath was made for man and that the Son of man is its Lord.

chapters.title: The twelve appointed amid growing opposition

parts.text: Jesus heals a withered hand on the sabbath, grieving at hardened hearts, while Pharisees and Herodians begin plotting his death. Crowds from many regions press toward him for healing, and he silences unclean spirits that identify him. On a mountain he appoints twelve to be with him and to preach, heal, and cast out devils.

His friends think him beside himself, and scribes claim he acts through Beelzebub. Jesus replies that a divided kingdom cannot stand and that a strong man’s house is plundered only after he is bound. He warns about blasphemy against the Holy Ghost because they call his spirit unclean. When his family seeks him, he identifies those doing God’s will as his family.

chapters.title: Receiving the word and trusting its Lord

parts.text: Jesus teaches beside the sea through the parable of the sower. He explains that the seed is the word and that different soils portray rejection, shallow endurance, competing desires, and fruitful reception. His disciples receive understanding of the kingdom’s mystery. The lamp and measuring sayings urge attentive hearing, since what is hidden will be revealed.

Further parables compare God’s kingdom to seed growing beyond the farmer’s understanding and to a small mustard seed becoming a sheltering plant. Jesus explains his teaching privately to the disciples. Crossing the sea that evening, they encounter a violent storm while he sleeps. He stills wind and water, questions their fear and lack of faith, and leaves them amazed that creation obeys him.

chapters.title: Deliverance, healing, and a child raised

parts.text: In the Gadarenes’ country, Jesus meets a tormented man living among tombs. The unclean spirits identify themselves as Legion and beg to enter swine; the herd rushes into the sea. The restored man sits clothed and sane, but frightened residents ask Jesus to leave. Jesus sends the man home to tell what the Lord has done for him.

Jairus seeks help for his dying daughter. On the way, a woman suffering twelve years of bleeding touches Jesus’ clothes and is healed. He calls her forward and commends her faith. News then arrives that the girl has died, but Jesus tells Jairus to believe. Taking the child by the hand, he raises her and commands that she be given food.

Jesus’ own country takes offense at him, and he marvels at their unbelief. He sends the twelve in pairs to preach repentance, heal, and cast out devils, relying on hospitality. Herod hears of Jesus and fears John has risen. Mark recounts how Herodias used her daughter’s request at a banquet to secure John’s beheading despite Herod’s reluctance.

The returning apostles seek rest, but Jesus compassionately teaches the crowds and feeds five thousand men with five loaves and two fishes, leaving twelve baskets. After praying alone, he comes to the disciples walking on the sea and calms their fear; when he enters the boat, the wind stops. They still fail to understand the loaves. In Gennesaret, crowds bring their sick for healing.

chapters.title: God’s commandment and the heart’s uncleanness

parts.text: Pharisees and scribes question the disciples’ failure to follow traditional washing. Jesus answers that their traditions can nullify God’s command, illustrated by dedicating property as Corban to avoid supporting parents. Lip-service without a faithful heart is vain worship. He explains that uncleanness arises from evil within the heart, producing sinful thoughts and actions, rather than from food entering the body.

In the region of Tyre and Sidon, a Syrophenician woman asks deliverance for her daughter. Her answer about the dogs receiving children’s crumbs is followed by the child’s release from the devil. Returning through Decapolis, Jesus privately heals a deaf man with impaired speech. Despite his command for silence, people widely proclaim their amazement that he makes the deaf hear and the speechless speak.

chapters.title: Seeing clearly and following the suffering Christ

parts.text: Jesus feeds about four thousand people with seven loaves and a few fishes, leaving seven baskets. He refuses the Pharisees’ demand for a heavenly sign. When the disciples misunderstand his warning about the leaven of the Pharisees and Herod, he recalls both feedings and questions their lack of understanding. At Bethsaida, a blind man’s sight is restored through successive touches.

Near Cesarea Philippi, Peter identifies Jesus as the Christ. Jesus then teaches that he must suffer, be rejected, die, and rise again. He rebukes Peter for opposing this path. Disciples and crowd alike are called to deny themselves and take up the cross. Saving one’s life at the expense of Jesus and the gospel brings loss, and gaining the world cannot repay a lost soul.

chapters.title: Glory, struggling faith, and humble service

parts.text: Jesus is transfigured before Peter, James, and John; Moses and Elias appear, and the heavenly voice commands them to hear God’s beloved Son. Descending, they discuss resurrection and Elias. Jesus then delivers a boy whom the disciples could not help. The father cries that he believes yet needs help with unbelief, and Jesus teaches the disciples about prayer and fasting.

Jesus again predicts his death and resurrection, but the disciples do not understand. Their argument about greatness leads him to teach service and receiving children in his name. He forbids hindering a man acting in his name merely because he does not follow their group. Severe warnings against causing believers to stumble accompany calls to remove occasions of sin and live at peace.

chapters.title: The cost and character of discipleship

parts.text: Jesus teaches that marriage joins man and woman as one flesh and condemns divorce followed by remarriage as adultery. He welcomes children and says the kingdom must be received as a child. A rich man leaves sorrowful when told to give his possessions to the poor and follow Jesus. Trust in riches obstructs entry into the kingdom, though salvation is possible with God. Sacrifice for Christ brings reward, with persecution.

On the road to Jerusalem, Jesus again predicts his suffering and resurrection. James and John seek places of glory, but he redirects them toward suffering and service. He came to serve and give his life a ransom for many. Leaving Jericho, he restores blind Bartimeus’ sight, and the man follows him.

chapters.title: The king enters and the temple is challenged

parts.text: Jesus enters Jerusalem on a colt as people spread garments and branches and acclaim the coming kingdom of David. After inspecting the temple, he returns to Bethany. The next day he pronounces judgment on a leafy fig tree without fruit, then drives traders from the temple, declaring it a house of prayer for all nations rather than a den of thieves.

The disciples later find the tree withered. Jesus teaches faith in God, believing prayer, and forgiveness of others. Back in the temple, religious leaders demand the source of his authority. He asks whether John’s baptism came from heaven or men. Unwilling to answer because of the consequences either way, they receive no answer to their own demand.

chapters.title: God’s claim, the greatest commandments, and a widow

parts.text: Jesus tells of vineyard tenants who mistreat servants and kill the owner’s beloved son. Their judgment and replacement expose the leaders’ rejection, reinforced by the rejected cornerstone Scripture. He answers a tax trap by distinguishing what belongs to Cesar and to God, then corrects the Sadducees’ disbelief in resurrection by explaining God’s power and his relationship with the living patriarchs.

A scribe asks about the greatest commandment. Jesus answers with love for the one God and love for neighbor, and commends the scribe’s understanding. He then questions how David’s son is also David’s Lord and warns against self-important scribes who exploit widows. Watching the treasury, he honors a poor widow whose two mites (coins) represent all her livelihood.

chapters.title: Watchfulness amid trouble and the coming kingdom

parts.text: Jesus foretells the temple’s destruction and answers the disciples’ questions with warnings against deception. Wars and disasters are beginnings rather than the end itself. His followers face courts, beatings, and betrayal, but the Holy Ghost will supply their testimony, and the gospel must reach all nations. Daniel’s abomination signals urgent flight from Judea before unparalleled affliction, and false messiahs must not be believed.

After that tribulation, heavenly signs accompany the Son of man’s coming in power and his gathering of the elect. The fig tree teaches recognition, and Jesus affirms that his words will never pass away. Since the day and hour are known only to the Father, everyone must remain awake and faithful like servants awaiting their master’s unexpected return.

A woman anoints Jesus at Bethany, and he defends her action as preparation for burial. Judas arranges betrayal while the disciples prepare passover. At the meal, Jesus warns that one of the twelve will betray him and gives bread and the cup as his body and covenant blood. He predicts the disciples’ scattering and Peter’s three denials before the cock crows twice.

In Gethsemane, Jesus prays in anguish yet submits to his Father’s will; the disciples sleep. Judas arrives with the arresting crowd, and Jesus is abandoned, including by a young man who escapes without his garment. Before the high priest, conflicting witnesses fail, but Jesus’ declaration of his identity and coming authority leads to condemnation and abuse. Peter denies him, then remembers the warning and weeps.

chapters.title: The crucified King and his burial

parts.text: The council delivers Jesus to Pilate, who is astonished by his silence under accusation. Though aware of the chief priests’ envy, Pilate satisfies the crowd by releasing Barabbas and sending Jesus to crucifixion. Soldiers clothe Jesus in purple, crown him with thorns, and mock his kingship before leading him away.

Simon of Cyrene is compelled to carry the cross. Jesus is crucified at Golgotha between thieves while onlookers and leaders mock him. Darkness comes over the land, and he cries to God before dying. The temple veil tears, and a centurion acknowledges God’s Son. Women watch from a distance. After Pilate confirms his death, Joseph of Arimathea wraps and buries him in a rock-cut tomb.

chapters.title: The risen Lord sends his witnesses

parts.text: Women bring spices to Jesus’ tomb after the sabbath and find the great stone already moved. Inside, a young man in white announces that the crucified Jesus has risen. They must tell the disciples, specifically including Peter, that he will meet them in Galilee. The women leave trembling and afraid.

Jesus appears to Mary Magdalene and to two disciples traveling in the country, but their reports are not believed. He then rebukes the eleven for unbelief and commissions them to preach the gospel throughout the world, speaking of belief, baptism, and accompanying signs. He is received into heaven and sits at God’s right hand. The disciples preach everywhere, with the Lord confirming the word through signs.
